run.question:
Alertmanager alert PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus since 2026-11-16T13:46:59Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The warning is structural, not a runtime crash: Prometheus prometheus/prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 (Pod IP 100.96.5.74:9090, matching the alert's instance) is running and ready, but the cluster contains no Alertmanager workload at all — no Alertmanager StatefulSet, Pod, Service or Endpoints in any of the 15 namespaces — so Prometheus has zero Alertmanagers to connect to and PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers is true by construction. The alertmanagers.monitoring.coreos.com CRD is installed and the prometheus-operator is healthy and reconciling (it regenerated the Prometheus rulefiles ConfigMap at 13:40:05Z), so nothing failed to deploy: the kube-prometheus-stack release simply runs without an Alertmanager instance. The alert's start at 13:46:59Z follows the Prometheus Pod recreation at 13:46:27Z by about 31 seconds, which explains the timing of the firing but not the condition. The only object in the cluster exposing the Alertmanager default port 9093 is the otel-demo Kafka Service (port name 'controller'), which is unrelated. The reachable Prometheus stores no prometheus_notifications_* or alertmanager_* series and has no job named prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus, so the exact series value that fired the rule could not be read independently; its TSDB also starts at 13:51:59Z, after the restart, so pre-restart history is unavailable.

claims.text: Pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 in namespace prometheus is Running with both containers ready (prometheus quay.io/prometheus/prometheus:v3.6.0 and config-reloader prometheus-config-reloader:v0.85.0), 0 restarts, containers started 2026-11-16T13:46:28Z, podIP 100.96.5.74 (matching the alert's instance 100.96.5.74:9090), owned by StatefulSet prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.

The cluster runs exactly 6 StatefulSets: chi-clickhouse-main-0-0 (clickhouse), jaeger-traces-recorder and prometheus-alert-recorder (data-recorders), topology-monitor (kube-system), opensearch-cluster-master (opensearch) and prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus (prometheus); none is an Alertmanager StatefulSet.

Among all 52 Endpoints objects, the only endpoint exposing TCP port 9093 (Alertmanager's default port) is the kafka Service in namespace otel-demo (port name 'controller', address 100.96.5.239); among all 66 Pods, only kafka-ff7884766-f4jgr declares containerPort 9093.

The cluster has 15 namespaces (agent, clickhouse, clickhouse-operator, data-recorders, default, ingress-nginx, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, metrics-server, opensearch, opentelemetry-collectors, opentelemetry-operator, otel-demo, prometheus); none is an alertmanager or monitoring namespace.

Namespace prometheus contains 5 Services (prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator, prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus, prometheus-kube-state-metrics, prometheus-operated, prometheus-prometheus-node-exporter), 2 Deployments (prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator, prometheus-kube-state-metrics) and 8 Pods (operator, kube-state-metrics, prometheus-0, five node-exporter pods); none is Alertmanager-related.

The alertmanagers.monitoring.coreos.com CRD (kind Alertmanager, group monitoring.coreos.com) is installed, so an Alertmanager instance is a supported kind in this cluster, but no such instance is materialized as a workload.

The prometheus-operator is healthy and reconciling: Pod prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator-57d68989cc-hkbnh runs prometheus-operator:v0.85.0 (started 2026-11-15T14:32:59Z, 0 restarts), and the operator-generated ConfigMap prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0 was (re)created 2026-11-16T13:40:05Z holding the Prometheus rule-file set.

Other kube-prometheus-stack components are running: kube-state-metrics Pod prometheus-kube-state-metrics-7c5fb9d798-tqssx (v2.17.0) and all five prometheus-prometheus-node-exporter DaemonSet pods have containers started 2026-11-15T14:32:59Z with 0 restarts.

The Prometheus StatefulSet prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus reports readyReplicas 1/1, generation 1, created 2026-11-15T14:32:59Z, with currentRevision equal to updateRevision prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-677d847d59, i.e. no template rollout occurred.

Alerts in this environment are collected from the Prometheus HTTP API rather than from an Alertmanager: Pod prometheus-alert-recorder-0 in namespace data-recorders sets PROMETHEUS_ENDPOINT=http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090.

Series in the reachable Prometheus start at 2026-11-16T13:51:59Z (source_start_at of count(otelcol_process_cpu_seconds_total)), i.e. after the Prometheus Pod recreation at 13:46:27Z, so no pre-restart samples exist in the query window.

The reachable Prometheus' job label has only three values — kube-state-metrics, kubelet, otel-collector — with no job named prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus (the alert's job label) and no Alertmanager scrape job.

Primary explanation: the kube-prometheus-stack release in namespace prometheus was deployed without any Alertmanager instance, so Prometheus prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus discovers zero Alertmanagers and PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers is true by construction rather than because Prometheus or an Alertmanager failed at runtime.

The alert's start at 2026-11-16T13:46:59Z, about 31s after the Prometheus container start at 13:46:28Z, is consistent with the rule first being evaluated or armed after the Pod was recreated; the restart explains the alert's start time but not the standing absence of an Alertmanager, which is independent of the restart.

Unresolved alternative: Prometheus' generated alerting configuration could reference an Alertmanager endpoint (for example alertmanager-operated in some namespace) whose backing workload never existed or was removed; the effective configuration lives in a Secret that cannot be read, so an empty alerting list versus a dangling Alertmanager reference cannot be distinguished from the available evidence.

Rejected: an Alertmanager Pod crashed, was OOMKilled, evicted or is in CrashLoopBackOff. No Alertmanager Pod or StatefulSet exists anywhere in the cluster (only the six enumerated StatefulSets, and no pod declaring port 9093 other than Kafka), so there is no failing Alertmanager component behind this alert.

Rejected: the alert is an artifact of Prometheus itself being down or unready. Pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 is Running, both containers are ready with 0 restarts, and the Prometheus container has been running since 2026-11-16T13:46:28Z.

Rejected: the alert is caused by a missing or mislabeled Service for Prometheus itself. Service prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus exists with ClusterIP 100.66.168.187 and port http-web 9090 (targetPort 9090), and the headless Service prometheus-operated also exposes http-web 9090, both selecting app.kubernetes.io/name=prometheus; the alert concerns Alertmanager connectivity, not Service reachability.

gaps: The effective Prometheus configuration (alerting.alertmanagers) is stored in a Secret that cannot be read, so whether the alerting section is truly empty or names a non-existent Alertmanager endpoint is unverified.

Network isolation could not be assessed: the NetworkPolicy query returned status no_data (0 items returned by that view), which is a stated limit of what this Run observed, not proof that no network policy exists; a policy blocking Prometheus-to-Alertmanager traffic therefore remains neither confirmed nor excluded.

The change_history integration is not available, so it cannot be determined whether an Alertmanager CR or workload ever existed and was removed before 2026-11-16T13:46; the reachable Prometheus' TSDB only begins at 2026-11-16T13:51:59Z.

Pod logs for prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 (init-config-reloader, prometheus, config-reloader) and for the prometheus-operator returned 0 lines, and namespace prometheus returned no Events; cluster-wide Events cover only 13:54:19Z-14:27:05Z and none references alertmanager or prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0. These views were no_data, so no application-side log or event conclusion can be drawn.

The reachable Prometheus holds no prometheus_notifications_* or alertmanager_* series and no series with job=prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus, so prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered could not be read; the alert payload remains the only evidence of the rule's evaluation.

The Alertmanager-named ConfigMap, Deployment, Service and StatefulSet sweeps all returned no_data (0 matching items per view); combined with the full 6-StatefulSet, 66-Pod, 52-Service and 52-Endpoints enumerations that show no Alertmanager, the absence is well supported for the query time but cannot be proven for the whole incident window.

Why the Prometheus Pod was recreated at 2026-11-16T13:46:27Z is unknown: the owning StatefulSet is still generation 1 with unchanged currentRevision/updateRevision, so this was not a controller-driven template rollout.

Whether alert delivery is expected to an off-cluster or external Alertmanager, and therefore what delivery is currently lost, could not be established; the otel-demo application services were not examined for impact because no evidence ties them to this alert.
next_steps: Verify the kube-prometheus-stack release values (alertmanager.enabled) and whether an Alertmanager resource exists in namespace prometheus; if alert delivery is required, deploy an Alertmanager instance so the operator materializes its StatefulSet and governing Service.

Read the Prometheus CR spec.alerting.alertmanagers and the generated Secret for prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus to confirm whether the alerting section is empty or references a stale endpoint.
If alerts are meant to be sent to an external Alertmanager, confirm its endpoint and DNS reachability from namespace prometheus.
Re-run a NetworkPolicy check against namespace prometheus and the cluster during the incident window to close the network-isolation gap.
Use Kubernetes audit logs to determine what deleted or recreated the prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 Pod at 2026-11-16T13:46:27Z.
